input_sentence: The 2026 FIFA World Cup kicks off at Estadio Azteca on June 11, 2026.
headline: 2026 FIFA World Cup Is Underway: Mexico Opens With a 2-0 Win as History Is Made at the Azteca
dek: The largest World Cup in history — 48 teams, 104 matches, three host nations — kicked off June 11 in Mexico City with a drama-filled opener full of goals, red cards, and a star-studded ceremony.
summary: The 2026 FIFA World Cup officially began on June 11 at the iconic Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, with co-host Mexico defeating South Africa 2-0 in a historic, drama-filled opener that saw three straight red cards — a first in any World Cup opening match. Julián Quiñones scored the tournament's first goal in the 9th minute, with Raúl Jiménez adding a second in the 66th. The tournament, jointly hosted by the United States, Mexico, and Canada, is the first to feature 48 teams and 104 matches and will run through July 19. On Day 2, Canada faced Bosnia and Herzegovina in Toronto, and the U.S. Men's National Team played Paraguay in Los Angeles.

key_facts.value: 48 teams divided into 12 groups; 104 matches across 16 host cities in the US, Mexico, and Canada

key_facts.label: Historic venue
key_facts.value: Estadio Azteca became the first stadium to host opening matches at three FIFA World Cups (1970, 1986, 2026)

key_facts.label: Defending champion
key_facts.value: Argentina, led by Lionel Messi, enters as defending champion and FIFA's top-ranked team

key_facts.label: World Cup final
key_facts.value: Final scheduled for July 19 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey

key_facts.label: Youngest player
key_facts.value: 17-year-old Mexican midfielder Gilberto Mora is the youngest player at the tournament

key_facts.label: Opening ceremony performers
key_facts.value: Shakira, J Balvin, Alejandro Fernández, Tyla, Burna Boy, Andrea Bocelli and EJAE performed at the Azteca ceremony

why_it_matters: This is the largest FIFA World Cup ever staged — the first with 48 teams, the first co-hosted by three nations, and the first to spread across North America. The expanded format (104 matches, a new Round of 32) gives more nations a path to the title and transforms the tournament into a nearly six-week continental spectacle. For Mexico, the US, and Canada, it represents a massive cultural and economic moment, while for football globally it sets the template for how the sport's biggest event will look for decades to come.
whats_next: USA Men's National Team (USMNT) plays its first match against Paraguay on June 12 at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles.
Canada's home opener vs. Bosnia and Herzegovina in Toronto on June 12 — the first World Cup match ever played by Canada on home soil.
Mexico's second group stage match: Czech Republic vs. Mexico at Estadio Azteca on June 24.
Watch for whether any of the five Day-1 scorers (Quiñones, Jiménez, Krejčí, Hwang In-beom, Oh Hyeon-gyu) build on their early tournament tallies.
Round of 32 begins July 4–7, cutting the field from 32 to 16.
World Cup Final halftime show on July 19 will feature Shakira, Madonna, and BTS co-headlining.

extras.format_summary: 48 teams are divided into 12 groups of four; the top two from each group plus the eight best third-place finishers (32 teams total) advance to a new Round of 32, then proceed through single-elimination knockout rounds to the final. Tied knockout matches go to 30 minutes of extra time and then a penalty shootout.
